title: Protocol for analyzing transforming growth factor β signaling in dextran-sulfate-sodium-induced colitic mice using flow cytometry and western blotting
protocol: Dissect the entire length of the colon by making an incision at the anus and another immediately below the cecum.
Wash the colon briefly in 1× PBS to remove excess blood.
Remove fecal contents from the colon using forceps.
Clean the forceps after each sample.
Remove as much fat attached to the colon as possible with forceps.
Cut the colon vertically and fold it open to expose the lumen.
Transfer the opened colon into a 50 mL conical tube containing ice-cold Buffer A.
Vortex the tube for 10 seconds and store it on ice.
Add pre-warmed Buffer C containing DTT to a 25 cm² flask.
Briefly vortex each 50 mL tube with colon tissue in Buffer A and then pour it over a metal tea strainer placed on a large beaker.
Lay the colon tissue flat on a paper towel for a few seconds to remove any remaining buffer.
Transfer the colon tissue to the flask containing 7.5 mL of pre-warmed Buffer C with DTT.
Firmly close the flasks now containing the tissue with caps and cover them tightly with parafilm to prevent leakage.
Horizontally place the sealed flasks with the colons into a 37°C incubating shaker immediately and secure them using tape to prevent them from falling.
Incubate for 20 min in the incubator at a shaking speed of 180 rpm.
If the incubator isn’t at 37°C prior to adding samples, add 5 extra minutes to each incubation.
During the incubation, thaw the Liberase and DNase I aliquots at 37°C.
Once thawed, prepare 10 mL per mouse of the enzyme solution (scale up as needed).
Keep the enzyme solution at 37°C.
When the incubation is over, place the flasks on ice immediately to stop the reaction.
Lay the colon tissue on a paper towel for a few seconds to remove buffer.
Transfer the colon tissue to another 50 mL conical tube containing 10 mL of ice-cold Buffer A.
Vortex briefly, then pour buffer and colon over the tea strainer.
Transfer the colon tissue to a 2 mL Eppendorf tube.
Chop each tissue with a pair of clean scissors for 1.5 min.
Take care not to scratch the bottom or sides of the tube while chopping colonic tissue.
Wipe scissors between samples with paper towels and clean buffer.
Add 900 μL of cold Buffer B to each tube.
Dip the scissors in the suspension to remove any remaining tissue pieces.
Keep tubes on ice until all samples are processed.
Finger-flick the tube and check for large tissue pieces after chopping.
Chop any remaining large tissue pieces for another minute or two.
Spin down Eppendorf tubes with tissue at 2,800 × g for 1 min at 4°C in a microcentrifuge.
Remove the supernatant and fat floating at the top using a P1000 pipette.
Resuspend the pellet with 1 mL of pre-warmed Enzyme Solution.
Vortex to disrupt the pellet and pour the suspension into a new 7.5 mL flask.
Repeat resuspension step three times, each time adding 1 mL of Enzyme Solution for a total of 3 mL per tissue.
Add 7 mL of pre-warmed Enzyme Solution to each flask to bring the final volume to 10 mL per tissue sample.
Incubate flasks at 37 °C at 120 rpm for 40 min.
Add 10 mL of ice-cold Buffer A into a separate 50 mL tube with a 100 μm cell strainer on top.
Keep the mixture on ice.
Transfer and pass the suspension through the 100 μm cell strainer tube using a 10 mL pipette once the incubation is finished.
Wash each flask with 10 mL of ice-cold Buffer A to catch any remaining tissue and transfer it over the corresponding cell strainer/tube for each tissue.
Mash the colon tissue over the 100 μm cell strainer using the plunger from a 1 mL syringe until it is passed through.
Discard any white membranous tissue left on the cell strainer.
Add 10 mL of ice-cold Buffer A to wash each cell strainer/tube and discard the cell strainer after use.
Return the top to the 50 mL tube to seal and spin down the samples for 5 min at 500 × g at 4°C in a table-top centrifuge.
Discard the supernatant quickly.
Resuspend the pellet with 10 mL of ice-cold Buffer A using a 10 mL pipette.
Transfer the suspension over a 50 mL conical tube with a 40 μm cell strainer and wash each cell strainer with 10 mL of ice-cold Buffer A.
Bring the final volume up to 30 mL with ice-cold Buffer A.
Spin down the samples for 5 min at 500 × g at 4°C in a table-top centrifuge.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Proceed with the pellet to the next steps for staining with antibodies and sorting for DCs and CD4+ T cells by FACS.
Resuspend the pellet in a 50 mL conical tube with 250 μL FACS buffer.
Add 10 μL of FcR Block Reagent (TruStain FcX) to each sample.
Incubate at 4°C for 10 min.
Add 2.5 μL of each antibody (CD4 – FITC, CD45 – BV421, I-Ab – PE, CD11c – APC) and 12.5 μL of 7-AAD to the cells in the 50 mL conical tube.
Pipette up and down to mix.
Incubate at 4°C for 30 min in the dark.
Add 1 mL of FACS buffer to each sample in a 50 mL conical tube.
Mix the solution by pipetting up and down.
Spin down the samples at 500 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant from the tubes.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Pass the cell suspension through a Corning cell strainer snap cap on a 5 mL polystyrene round-bottom tube.
Place the samples on ice.
Sort CD11c+ DCs and CD4+ T cells using a FACSAria IIu flow cytometer.
Spin down the sorted cells at 500 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant from the tubes.
Resuspend the cells in FACS buffer or RIPA buffer.
Proceed with intracellular staining and western blotting for phosphorylated Smad2/3 and Smad7.
Transfer cells to a 96-well round bottom plate.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 420 × g.
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 100 μL of 1× fixable LIVE/DEAD stain (Zombie Aqua Fixable Viability Dye).
Incubate for 10 min at 37°C.
Wash cells by adding 100 μL of PBS.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 420 × g.
Discard supernatant.
Fix cells by resuspending in 100 μL 2% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS.
Incubate at 37°C for 10 min.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 420 × g.
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 100 μL of ice-cold methanol.
Incubate at 4°C for 60 min in the dark.
Wash cells by adding 200 μL FACS buffer.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 420 × g.
Discard supernatant.
Wash cells again by adding 200 μL FACS buffer.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 420 × g.
Discard supernatant.
Perform intracellular staining by resuspending cells in 100 μL FACS buffer containing 2 μL of phospho-Smad2/3 antibody.
Incubate for 60 min at RT.
Wash cells by adding 100 μL FACS buffer.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 420 × g.
Discard supernatant.
Wash cells again by adding 200 μL FACS buffer.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 420 × g.
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 200 μL FACS Buffer.
Transfer to tubes compatible with your flow cytometer’s sample injection port.
Store at 4°C until samples are acquired on a flow cytometer.
Keep cells on ice and protected from light until sorting begins.
Centrifuge cell samples at 1,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Wash the pellet with PBS.
Remove supernatant and add 200 μL RIPA lysis buffer containing 1× complete mini proteinase inhibitor cocktail per 10^6 cells.
Incubate cell lysate on ice for 1 hour with vortexing every 15 minutes.
Pass through a bent 27-gauge needle 10 times.
Sonicate for 10 cycles at 40% amplitude with 1-second pulse and 10 seconds off on the ice.
Centrifuge samples at 20,000 × g for 30 minutes.
Collect supernatant to obtain whole cell lysate.
Measure protein concentration using Bradford Protein Assay Kit according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Adjust protein concentration to 5 μg/μL with RIPA lysis buffer.
Store adjusted protein samples at -80°C.
Take 30–50 μg total protein and add 6 × loading buffer.
Make up the volume to 10 μL using lysis buffer.
Heat the prepared sample at 100°C for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge heated sample at 7,000 × g for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Load 10 μL of protein sample per lane on a gradient 4%–20% SDS-PAGE gel.
Load 10 μL of pre-stained protein standard as a marker.
Run the SDS-PAGE gel at 100 V until markers are separated.
Immerse blotting papers in transfer buffer for 10 minutes or more.
Take out the gel and immerse it in the transfer buffer.
Rock the gel gently for 5–10 minutes.
Place the PVDF membrane gently on top of the gel.
Place blotting papers on both sides of the PVDF membrane and the gel.
Carefully remove bubbles using a roller.
Transfer proteins onto the PVDF membrane at 300 mA for 60 minutes using the wet transfer apparatus.
Wash the PVDF membrane twice in Tris buffered saline with 0.1% Tween 20 (TBST).
Block the PVDF membrane with 5% non-fat milk in TBST at room temperature for 60 minutes on a rocker.
Incubate the PVDF membrane with Smad7 antibody (1:500 dilution) or GAPDH (1:5000 dilution) or α-tubulin (1:5000 dilution) in 5% non-fat milk in TBST overnight at 4°C.
Rinse the PVDF membrane twice with PBST after incubation with the primary antibody.
Wash the membrane thrice with TBST at room temperature for 10 minutes on a rocker.
Incubate the PVDF membrane with the secondary antibody conjugated with HRP in 5% non-fat milk in TBST (1:5,000 dilution) at room temperature for 1 hour on a rocker.
Rinse the PVDF membrane twice with TBST after incubation with the secondary antibody.
Wash the PVDF membrane thrice by TBST at room temperature for 10 minutes each.
Decant the TBST and add the Luminata HRP reagent.
Incubate the PVDF membrane for 5 minutes with the Luminata HRP reagent.
Image on the G:Box ChemiXX6/XX9 – High-resolution gel imaging system.
Export images in 300 dpi tiff format for creating the figures.
